report:
**Decision: adopt the graft; drop the parent's separate per-call writer.**

Source+native alone cannot attribute: without SDK metadata they identify neither the model turn nor a durable route, and the same intent/started series also serves host `bounded()` calls (post-prompt protected check). Code hash-binding proves the task, not the route/call at kill time.

Graft spec:
1. `pi-model-invocation.json`, real only: caller runtimeSource immediately after route/tool validation, before `session.prompt`. Fields: version, attemptId, taskSha256, provider/model/effort/thinkingLevel, callableTools, providerPromptStarted:true. No auth, paths, commands, text. Same atomic pattern (wx temp, fsync, link, dir fsync), write-once; write failure aborts before prompt.
2. Metadata, real only: in `tool.execute` after abort/limit/canary checks, immediately before `bounded`: `{sdkCallSha256: sha256(_id), operation, invocationSha256}` as optional fourth arg bounded→nativeRun, spread into the existing binding for both intent and started. `seq` remains the ordinal. Offline callers pass nothing, so offline bytes and verifications stay unchanged.
3. Semantics: metadata persists before spawn/release, so no effect lacks it; host calls carry none and reviewers exclude them; claim kill only when `started` exists. `inspectNativeRecovery` ignores extra keys; the receipt hashes records, transitively binding invocationSha. No framework, no admission change; charge stays unreconciled.

Sufficient claim: validated route prompted; SDK call H executed as native seq N under task T.
